summary.value: A farming and pollination common — the hero calls it a battlefield. Its resident cast: swarmers bat-moss, wasp-yellowjacket, and moth-plague; chasers zombie-shambler and frog-bog; the cultist-acolyte shooters (gardeners, in truth); bomber shroom-violet; sniper spider-forest; and turret shroom-earth. When the bells ring, these are the neighbors who arrive to contain the intruder — volunteers first, then wardens, then specialists, then a Heavy Hand.

sharedOpinions.reason: He tramples the pollination rows and calls our harvesters a horde. The pauses between our waves shrink because the whole valley keeps arriving to help.
Their groves take our spores; our pollinators service their saplings. We are one long growing season apart.
They trade lantern oil for spore-flour every autumn and always overstay for the harvest dance.
A barn fire or a collapsed root cellar brings them over the hill before the smoke does. Their seal means help; the hero thinks it means loot.

examples.value: You do not own a field; you borrow it from next year.
Bad news travels like spores — everywhere, and before you see it coming.

meaning.value: Shared ground worked by everyone and owned by no one. The hero hears 'battlefield'; the residents hear 'lunch'.
The emergency muster when the warning bells ring — residents drop tools and walk toward the trouble, in the order the bells call them.

customs.value: First baskets of every harvest go to the commons storehouse before any private larder. No one in the valley has gone hungry in living memory.
Whoever rings the warning bell stays to direct the arrivals. You summon help, you organize it.

taboos.value: Never take from the commons storehouse without logging it. The hero's 'treasure detour' is our winter food.
Never cut across a planted row, whatever the hurry. Fences here are suggestions; rows are law.
